summary: CRT-style stream close (cdecl on a stream struct). Reads the OS file-handle index a1[4] (field +0x10), locks the stream, flushes buffered writes, clears control bits in the stream flags a1[3] (field +0xC), resets the per-handle buffer descriptor (the default unk_5E7898 when the handle is -1, otherwise a descriptor addressed as dword_8D4920[v1 >> 5] + 36 * (v1 & 0x1F)), clears bit 1 of that descriptor, clears the low two bits of the flags when bit 7 (0x80) is set, closes the OS handle via sub_58C724(v1, 0, 0), and releases the stream through AddressRangeCriticalSectionLeave.

local_names.v1: OS file-handle index read from a1[4]; -1 means no handle attached
local_names.v3: stream flags copy used for the 0x80 guard

operations.description: Read the file-handle index v1 = a1[4] (field +0x10); -1 means no OS handle is attached.
Lock the stream for exclusive access via StreamBufferLockViaCriticalSection(a1).
Flush pending buffered write data via BufferFlushWrite(a1).
Clear control bits in the stream flags: a1[3] &= 0xFFFFFFCF (field +0xC).
If v1 == -1 use the default buffer descriptor unk_5E7898; otherwise resolve the per-handle buffer descriptor from dword_8D4920[v1 >> 5] + 36 * (v1 & 0x1F).
Clear bit 1 of the buffer descriptor flags: v2[4] &= ~2u.
If the stream flags have bit 7 set ((a1[3] & 0x80u) != 0), clear the low two bits: a1[3] = a1[3] & 0xFC (field +0xC).
Close the OS file handle via sub_58C724(v1, 0, 0).
Release the stream and its critical-section slot via AddressRangeCriticalSectionLeave(a1).
Called by sub_5354E0 (0x005354E0) as part of its stream teardown path.

unresolved: Semantic interpretation (CRT fclose behavior) is from the corpus fill; the packet does not define what unk_5E7898, the dword_8D4920 descriptor-array layout (36-byte stride, index v1 >> 5 and v1 & 0x1F), the flag bits in a1[3] and v2[4], or the constant arguments (0, 0) to sub_58C724 mean.
Whether AddressRangeCriticalSectionLeave also frees the stream structure is from the corpus fill, not the packet.
The 0xFFFFFFCF and 0xFC masks on a1[3] and the ~2u mask on v2[4] clear specific flag bits whose meanings are not defined by the packet.
